title: A rational third-slice isomorphism extends to an open neighbourhood
statement: Let K be a field [def-weil-field], X,Y,Z schemes over K [def-weil-scheme-over-base], X,Y proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and x,y,z rational points of X,Y,Z [def-pc-rational-point]. Let M,N be invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] on X×Y×Z [def-pc-fibre-product]. If M and N have isomorphic pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback] on each of {x}×Y×Z, X×{y}×Z and X×Y×{z}, then there is an open neighbourhood U of the underlying point of z in Z over whose inverse image M and N are isomorphic.

source.place: Tags 0BF3 and 0BF4, rational third slice; source-library theorem of the cube interface

proof.text: Set L=M⊗N∨ and t=z(closedPoint K). Tensoring each slice isomorphism with the dual gives triviality of L on all three slices. The canonical map Spec κ(t)→Z factors through the K-point z: its residue-field map κ(t)→K is a field homomorphism with a right inverse induced by the structure morphism, hence is bijective. Cancel its Spec isomorphism in the defining factorization of z to obtain this equality.

Let i:X×Y→X×Y×Z be the third-slice morphism and let q be the first projection composed with p.fiberι(t). The previous factorization gives q≫i=p.fiberι(t), as verified on both product projections. Pull the third-slice trivialization back along q to trivialize L on the entire residue-field fibre at t.
Apply the arbitrary-fibre openness lemma to L, using the first two slice trivializations and the fibre trivialization just constructed. It gives U containing t on which L is trivial.

Use the tensor-dual cancellation equivalence to turn this trivialization into an isomorphism of the restrictions of M and N. The point t is the underlying point occurring in the conclusion, so U is the required neighbourhood.
